doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Reacting to segregation in America
summary: Brown asks if he was shocked by segregation; Toots says he wanted to be in Black parts of cities.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I want to ask you a serious, something about a very serious subject, because you talked about something that, kind of in passing, but I think is important. You talked about you and the vibist going out and taking the orders. This was because of the race relations in America.
Was that something shocking to you when you first encountered it? Or what was your reaction when you first…
…realized that in America, there were two separate, two separate Americas?

Yes. There was. Well, but I must be honest. All the musicians or the Europeans that came to the States, and I was anxious to be in the, in the black, you know, parts of the world or the city or… Back in Los Angeles there was still the Watts Hotel in Watts, you know. Yeah, that’s…
Were you surprised or did you know that that was the way it was?
